eyebrow: Every pushed tag, listed on its own
caption: Real Docker Hub Tags tab -- each tag gets its own pull command, digest, and size, independent of every other tag on the same repository.

code:
$ docker build -t northbridgeretail/catalog:1.5 .
$ docker tag northbridgeretail/catalog:1.5 northbridgeretail/catalog:latest
$ docker tag northbridgeretail/catalog:1.5 northbridgeretail/catalog:a1b2c3d

$ docker push northbridgeretail/catalog:1.5
$ docker push northbridgeretail/catalog:latest
$ docker push northbridgeretail/catalog:a1b2c3d
caption: docker tag doesn't copy data -- all three tags point at the exact same image ID.

steps.label: Semver (1.5)
steps.sub: a deliberate release number -- major.minor.patch, bumped on purpose

steps.label: latest
steps.sub: convenience pointer to the newest push -- fine for dev, never safe to deploy by

steps.label: Git-SHA (a1b2c3d)
steps.sub: the exact commit that built the image, traceable straight to source

code:
# A bug in 1.5? Cut 1.5.1 -- never re-push 1.5.
$ docker build -t northbridgeretail/catalog:1.5.1 .
$ docker push northbridgeretail/catalog:1.5.1

$ docker pull northbridgeretail/catalog:a1b2c3d
Status: Downloaded newer image for northbridgeretail/catalog:a1b2c3d
caption: A git-sha tag returns identical bytes today and a year from now -- the whole reason production deploys pin to one, never to latest.

subtitle: Docker Hub isn't the only registry -- Northbridge also pushes to Azure and AWS's own managed ones.
